# SPEC 2.2 uses "walk" as its own normative term (Rule A6). The specification is frozen and these lines stay.
# The two Satoshi Hike 2.0 allowlist entries named a file this tree no longer has.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	**Asynchronous model.** The walk is the back-to-back run of legs from the seed to the final interrupt. Every waypoint post, Hashcash solve, path ask, peer or header-source read, Bari exchange, and log write is an asynchronous event. None of them pauses a leg (Rule A6). The one read on the walk path is the tip read after each checkpoint, and it never waits. A run ends only at the final interrupt, on a producer failure, or on explicit cancellation.

Produce logs it (section 13.5) and the walk continues. An unsuccessful Hashcash, POST, or path-ask read is a miss, and produce continues. A run ends only at `I_17`, on a producer failure, or on explicit cancellation. | §9, Rule A6 |
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	| P9.16 | CONSTANT | On the live plane the header source keeps at least `HEADER_PEERS_MIN` 2 gossip peers. A connected peer that has not announced a header within `HEADER_PEER_SILENCE_SECONDS` 120 of another connected peer announcing it is replaced. Below 2 peers the source reconnects asynchronously with backoff and writes an `alert` `header_peers_low`; the walk and the object are unaffected. | §9 |
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	| A6 | INVARIANT | No post, Hashcash solve, ask, peer or header-source read, Bari exchange, or log write pauses, orders, delays, or interrupts a leg. Each is an asynchronous event. The post-checkpoint tip read stays on the walk path and never waits. | §13 Rule A6 |

spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	**Header source.** On the live plane the producer’s header source keeps sessions with at least `HEADER_PEERS_MIN` gossip peers at the same time, for the whole run. `HEADER_PEERS_MIN` is 2. A peer announces a header when it relays that header or a header that builds on it. When one connected peer has announced a header and another connected peer has not announced it within `HEADER_PEER_SILENCE_SECONDS` of the first announcement, the silent peer is disconnected and replaced by a new peer from the starting list or from addresses that peers have given. `HEADER_PEER_SILENCE_SECONDS` is 120. Both values are constants of this file. They are not levers and not SDK options. While no peer announces a new header, no peer is replaced: a natural gap between blocks is not silence. When fewer than `HEADER_PEERS_MIN` peers are connected, the header source keeps connecting new peers asynchronously, backing off between attempts, and writes an `alert` record (section 13.5) named `header_peers_low` each time the count falls below `HEADER_PEERS_MIN`. The walk continues, the object is unaffected, and the run still follows this section. A header source built to use one peer does not follow this section. Keeping, replacing, and reconnecting peers is asynchronous work and never pauses a leg (Rule A6). The copied list is checked again against Bitcoin Core's mainnet chainparams when a producer release is cut.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	A clock read that does not succeed never stops the run and never withholds the object. A post-checkpoint tip read that does not succeed is not an interrupt: the walk continues with its next leg, and produce logs the transitory condition (section 13.5). An Observe for the fee header, a waypoint POST, or a path ask that does not succeed is a miss. Rule A3.4 records it and produce continues.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	**Normative.** The walk is the back-to-back run of legs from the seed through `I_17`. Every waypoint post, Hashcash solve, path ask, peer or header-source read, Bari exchange, event-log write, and stderr write is an asynchronous event. No such event pauses, delays, orders, or interrupts a leg, and no leg waits for one to finish. The only read on the walk path is the post-checkpoint tip read (Rule A1.1), which returns at once the latest header the header source already holds. A failed read, a stalled header source, a Bari outage, a log that cannot be written, a slow peer, or any other transitory network condition is logged (section 13.5), and the walk continues. A run ends only at `I_17`, on a producer failure, or on explicit cancellation. Bugs are producer failures; they are not covered by this rule. Asynchronous work may share the host’s CPU with legs. This rule does not change what a leg computes, and it does not permit any change to the terrain, the step, the fold, or the slot read.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	**Fee header.** When the post of `W_g` starts, the producer takes as fee header the 80-byte block header its header source holds as best tip. Its `header_hash` is `SHA-256(SHA-256(header))`, 32 bytes in natural order. Taking it is not a tip read of the walk, does not end a stage, and is not `I_g`. If the header source holds no header, the POST does not succeed: produce logs the miss and continues.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	6. **Alert.** When the run meets a transitory condition that does not stop it, for example a tip read that did not succeed, a header-source stall, a fee header that is not available, or a log append that did not succeed (written when appending works again, if it does). `event` is `hike.produce.alert`. `alert` is a short lowercase name of the condition, for example `clock_read_failed`, `header_source_stalled`, `fee_header_missing`, or `log_append_failed`. `stage` is the stage the walk was in. `height` is the height concerned, and is omitted when there is none. An alert is not an input to the hike and does not change the object.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	**Measuring method.** Measure on an owned commodity host. The low end of that set is the low-end owned host (an Intel Core i7-10610U laptop, no SHA-NI). Use a conforming SDK at the cut tag of this file (section 16.2) that passes the whole pack, including every permanent negative. Run a real beacon-paced hike under this file’s producer rules: nothing pauses a leg (Rule A6), and there is no wait before a path ask. The rate is the first-beacon to last-beacon rate, `hike_legs / hike_span`, Rule A4.10, with `hike_span` the median-time-past difference. The floor is calibrated on the best legal packed rate per machine. That rate is `N` parallel PCOCs with distinct keys. Distinct keys make distinct terrains under this seed. An interleave of those hikes is the packed rate. Shared-terrain packing across distinct PCOCs is impossible under this seed. It is not a legal schedule. Record the host, the CPU, the implementation, the commit, and that packed rate beside the single-hike rate. A policy that follows this method sets the floor a little below the low-end host’s rate. **The floor must be measured under this file.** A rate measured with a producer that paused the walk (for example, with a wait before path asks or a blocking post) is not a measurement for this file: those pauses sat inside `hike_span` and understate the rate a producer of this file reaches at the same cost per leg. This method informs the value a policy sets. It does not set one.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	An SDK producer runs the walk on its own thread or threads and runs every post, solve, ask, header-source read, Bari exchange, and log write as asynchronous work (Rule A6). The walk reads the tip through a call that returns at once. No SDK producer sleeps, waits on I/O, takes a lock that I/O holds, or syncs a file on the walk path. A failure of asynchronous work becomes an `alert` record or a logged miss; it never propagates into the walk. Only a producer failure or explicit cancellation ends a run before `I_17`. The header source detects a stalled or lagging peer and recovers on its own, asynchronously; a stall never pauses a leg.
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	| F5 | Waypoint post before the next stage’s legs (blocking post). | The walk waited on Bari and on the Hashcash solve, so legs paused at every boundary and the measured rate fell. | Rule A1.4 (post is asynchronous); Rule A6; Rule I3. |
spec/satoshi-hike-v2.2/SPEC.md	| F6 | The 15–45 s wait before each path ask. | It ran inside the walk and cost about 1,000 s per hike (7.6–8 %). Rates and the floor measured with it understate an honest producer. | Section 13.1 (an ask is sent when due, with no wait); P13.7; Rule A6; section 15.5 (re-measure the floor). |
